20	We sometimes refer to this as the ``classical low-degree test'' for short.
    21	The low-degree test is used as a subroutine in the Pauli Basis test (see
    22	Section~\ref{sec:pauli-verifier}) as well as the answer-reduction normal form
    23	verifier (see Section~\ref{sec:ans}).
    24	We describe the test as a nonlocal game in Section~\ref{sec:ld-game} and show
    25	that the question distribution can be implemented as a (typed) conditionally
    26	linear distribution (see \Cref{sec:types} for the definition of typed CL
    27	distributions).
    28	
    29	
    30	\subsubsection{The game}
    31	\label{sec:ld-game}
    32	
    33	The game $\game^\ld$ is parametrized by a tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$
    34	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
    35	and $m$ divides $q$.
    36	We sometimes write $\game^\ld_\ldparams$ to emphasize the dependence of the
    37	classical low-degree test on the parameter tuple $\ldparams$.
    38	
    39	We first provide a high-level description of the game for $k=1$.
    40	It is based on the low-individual degree variant of the multilinearity test
    41	of~\cite{babai1991non}, where one player (called the ``points player'') receives
    42	a random point $u \in \F_q^m$, and the other player (called the ``lines
    43	player'') receives a random axis-parallel line $\line$ that contains $u$, i.e.\
    44	the line parallel to the $i$-th axis which goes through point $u$, for uniformly
    45	random $i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$.
    46	The points player is supposed to respond with a value $a \in \F_q$, and the
    47	lines player is supposed to respond with a univariate polynomial $f_\line$ of
    48	degree at most $d$ such that $f_\line(u_i) = a$, where $u_i$ is the $i$-th
    49	coordinate of $u$.
    50	
    51	Suppose the players agree beforehand on a global polynomial $g: \F_q^m \to \F_q$
    52	such that every variable has degree at most $d$.
    53	Then a winning strategy is the following: the points player responds with
    54	$g(u)$, and the lines player responds with the univariate polynomial $f_\line$
    55	that is the restriction of $g$ to line $\line$; formally, for $t \in \F_q$,
    56	\[f_\line(t)=g(u_1,u_2,\ldots,u_{i-1},t,u_{i+1},\ldots,u_m)\;.\] It is easy to
    57	see that $f_\line(t)$ has degree at most $d$ in the variable $t$.
    58	Thus in this case the players will pass the low-degree test with probability
    59	$1$.
    60	The low-degree testing theorem states that the converse approximately holds: if
    61	the players pass the low-degree test with probability close to $1$, then their
    62	responses must be approximately consistent (in some sense) with a global
    63	polynomial $g$ with individual degree $d$.
    64	
    65	When $k > 1$, the players are supposed to respond with a \emph{tuple} of
    66	answers; and the test is intended to check that the players' responses are
    67	consistent with a $k$-tuple of functions $g_i: \F_q^m \to \F_q$ that are
    68	polynomials where every variable has degree at most $d$.
    69	
    70	The game that we use is slightly more elaborate than the ``axis-parallel
    71	lines-versus-points'' test just described.
    72	In addition, we have two other subtests.
    73	One is a ``diagonal line-vs-points'' test: here, the points player receives a
    74	point $u \in \F_q^m$ as before, but the lines player receives a line $\line$
    75	that goes through $u$ but is not necessarily axis-aligned.
    76	Instead, it's chosen by first picking an index $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$
    77	uniformly at random, picking $v \in \F_q^m$ uniformly at random, and letting $v'
    78	= \pi_{i-1}(v) = (0,0,\ldots,0,v_i,v_{i+1},\ldots,v_m)$ (i.e., $\pi_{i-1}$
    79	zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of its input).
    80	Then, the line is defined as the set
    81	\[
    82		\line = \{ u + tv' : t \in \F_q \}\;,
    83	\]
    84	which is a uniformly random line in the affine subspace of $\F^m_q$
    85	corresponding to all points $v$ whose first $(i-1)$ coordinates match those of
    86	$u$.
    87	The points player responds with a value $a \in \F_q$, the lines player responds
    88	with a univariate polynomial $f_\line$ of degree $md$,\footnote{Since $\line$ is
    89	  no longer axis-parallel, the restriction of an individual degree-$d$
    90	  polynomial $g$ to a line $\line$ may yield a degree $md$ polynomial.}
    91	and the verifier checks that $f_\line(t_u) = a$ (where $t_u \in \F_q$ is the
    92	projection of $u$ onto the line $\line$ with respect to a canonical
    93	parameterization of $\line$).
    94	
    95	The other additional test is a ``consistency test'', where both players receive
    96	either the same points question, the same axis-parallel lines question, or the
    97	same diagonal lines question.
    98	In all cases they are expected to respond with the same answer.
    99	
   100	
   101	
   102	\paragraph{Axis-parallel lines and diagonal lines.}
   103	Before presenting a formal description of the game $\game^\ld$, we first define
   104	what we mean by lines, and their properties.
   105	
   106	\begin{definition}[Lines]
   107	  \label{def:line}
   108		A \emph{line} $\line$ in $\F^m_q$ specified by a pair $(u,v) \in (\F_q^m)^2$
   109	  is the subset
   110	  \begin{equation}
   111	    \label{eq:line-set}
   112	    \line(u,v) = \bigl\{\, u + tv : t \in \F_q \,\bigr\} \subseteq \F_q^m \;.
   113	  \end{equation}
   114	  We call the vector $v$ a \emph{direction} of line
   115	  $\line(u,v)$.\footnote{For convenience we explicitly allow
   116	    $v=0$, in which case the line is reduced to a singleton.}
   117	  
   118	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{axis-parallel} if there is a coordinate $i \in
   119	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ for which $v$ is equal to $e_i$, the $i$-th elementary basis
   120	  vector in $\F_q^m$.
   121	  We say that such a line $\line$ is \emph{parallel to the $i$-th direction}.
   122	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{diagonal} if there exists an $i \in
   123	  \{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}$ for which $v_1 = v_2 = \cdots = v_i = 0$.
   124	\end{definition}
   125	
   126	The following Proposition establishes that, for a fixed direction, a line
   127	$\line$ is an equivalence class of points on the line.
   128	\begin{proposition}
   129	  \label{prop:line-equiv}
   130	  Let $u,v \in \F_q^m$.
   131	  Then for all $u' \in \line(u,v)$, we have that $\line(u,v) = \line(u',v)$.
   132	\end{proposition}
   133	\begin{proof}
   134		Fix $u' \in \line(u,v)$.
   135	  We have that $u' = u + tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$.
   136	  Let $a \in \line(u,v)$.
   137	  This means that $a = u + sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$.
   138	  We also have that $a = u + (s - t + t)v = u + tv + (s - t)v = u' + (s - t)v$,
   139	  so $\line(u,v) \subseteq \line(u',v)$.
   140	  A similar argument shows that $\line(u',v) \subseteq \line(u,v)$.
   141	\end{proof}
   142	
   143	We now specify a canonical representation of lines $\line = \line(u,v)$ as pairs $(u_0,v)$
   144	where $u_0$ is a \emph{canonical representative} of $\line$ specified as
   145	follows.
   146	Let $L_v^{\lnf}: \F_q^m \to \F_q^m$ denote the canonical linear map with the
   147	one-dimensional kernel basis $\{v\}$ (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical} for a
   148	definition of canonical linear map).
   149	Note that for all $u \in \line$, we have that $L_v^{\lnf}(u)$ is a point in
   150	$\line$.
   151	This is because since the image and kernel of $L_v^{\lnf}$ are complementary
   152	subspaces by definition (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical}), any $u \in \F_q^m$ has a
   153	unique decomposition $u = u_0 + u_1$ where $u_0$ is in the image of $L_v^{\lnf}$
   154	and $u_1 \in \ker(L_v^{\lnf})$, which by definition is the subspace spanned by
   155	$v$.
   156	Thus $u_1 = tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$ and we have that $u_0 = u - tv \in \line$.
   157	In particular, if $u\in \line$ then $u_0 = L_v^{\lnf}(u) \in \line$ as well. 
   158	Furthermore, since $L_v^{\lnf}$ is a projection onto its image by definition, we
   159	have $L_v^{\lnf}(u_0) = u_0$.
   160	
   161	Next, note that for any $u,u' \in \line$, since $u-u' = sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$
   162	it follows that $L_v^\lnf(u) = L_v^\lnf(u')$.
   163	Thus $u_0 = u_0'$ and this shows that $L_v^\lnf$ gives a means to compute a
   164	canonical representative of lines.
   165	
   166	\begin{definition}[Canonical representative of a line]
   167	  \label{def:line-representative}
   168	  Let $\line$ be a line in direction $v$.
   169	  A canonical representative of $\line$ is the point $u_0 \in \F_q^m$ such that
   170	  \[
   171	    u_0 = L_v^\lnf(u)
   172	  \]
   173	  for all $u \in \line$.
   174	\end{definition}
   175	
   176	
   177	
   178	\paragraph{Question distribution.}
   179	We now present the question distribution of the game $\game^\ld$ as a typed CL
   180	distribution (see \Cref{sec:types} for the definition of typed CL functions and
   181	typed CL distributions).
   182	The type set $\type^\ld$ of the game $\game^\ld$ we use is
   183	\[
   184		\type^\ld = \{ \Point, \ALine, \DLine \}\;.
   185	\]
   186	The distribution over question types is uniform over $\type^\ld \times \type^\ld$. 
   187	
   188	We introduce the corresponding typed CL functions $L_\Point$, $L_\ALine$,
   189	$L_\DLine$ where the corresponding CL distributions $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$
   190	and $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$ implement the axis line-versus-point and diagonal
   191	line-versus-point distributions, respectively.
   192	The functions are parametrized by a field size $q$, a dimension $m$, and three
   193	complementary register subspaces $V_\xpt,V_{\coord}, V_{\dir{}}$ of some ambient
   194	space.
   195	The register $V_\xpt$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$) is called the
   196	\emph{point register}, $V_\coord$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q$) is called the
   197	\emph{coordinate register}, and $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$)
   198	is called the \emph{direction register}, respectively.
   199	We let $V$ denote the direct sum $V_\xpt \oplus V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$.
   200	We identify elements of $V$ as triples $(u,s,v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q \times
   201	\F_q^m$.
   202	
   203	Define $L_\Point$ to be the $1$-level CL function that projects onto $V_\xpt$: for every $(u,s,v) \in V$,
   204	\begin{equation}
   205	  \label{eq:cl-ptf}
   206		L_\Point(u,s,v) = (u,0,0) \;.
   207	\end{equation}
   208	Define $L_\ALine$ to be the following $2$-level CL function:
   209	\begin{equation}
   210	  \label{eq:cl-alnf}
   211		L_\ALine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{e_i}(u), s, 0)\ \text{for all } (u,s,v) \in V,
   212	\end{equation}
   213	where $L^\lnf$ is the linear function used to compute the canonical
   214	representative of lines (see \Cref{def:line-representative}), and $i = \chi(s)$
   215	where we define $\chi(s)$ to be the unique integer such that
   216	\begin{equation}
   217	\label{eq:chi-func}
   218		s = (\chi(s) - 1) \frac{q}{m} + r
   219	\end{equation}
   220	for some $0 \leq r < q/m$, and we interpret the field element $s \in \F_q$ as an
   221	integer between $0$ and $q - 1$).
   222	The function $L_\ALine$ is the concatenation of the $1$-level CL function that
   223	projects the subspaces $V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ down to $V_\coord$ (i.e.
   224	zeroes out the entire $V_{\dir{}}$ register), and the family of $1$-level CL
   225	functions $\{L^\lnf_{e_i} \}$ acting on $V_\xpt$, indexed by $i \in
   226	\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   227	(See \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation.)
   228	Thus $L_\ALine$ is a $2$-level CL function.
   229	
   230	Define $L_\DLine$ to be the following $3$-level CL function: for all $(u,s,v) \in
   231	V$,
   232	\begin{equation}
   233	\label{eq:cl-dlnf}
   234		L_\DLine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{\pi_{i-1}(v)}(u),s,\pi_{i-1}(v))
   235	\end{equation}
   236	where $i = \chi(s)$.
   237	The function $L_\DLine$ is the concatenation of the following CL functions (again, see \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation): (i) the identity function on $V_{\coord}$ (which is a $1$-level CL function); (ii) for every $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ the $1$-level CL function on $V_{\dir{}}$ that maps $v \mapsto \pi_{i-1}(v)$ (i.e.~it zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of $v$), and (iii) for every pair $(s,v') \in V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$, the $1$-level CL function $L^\lnf_{v'}$ acting on $V_\xpt$. Thus $L_\DLine$ is a $3$-level CL function.
   238	
   239	
   240	The following two lemmas establish that the CL functions
   241	$L_\Point,L_\ALine,L_\DLine$ give rise to the axis-parallel line-versus-point and
   242	diagonal line-versus-point distributions.
   243	\begin{lemma}
   244		\label{lem:alnf}
   245		Consider the pair $(\line, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   246	  tuple $((u_0,s,0),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$,
   247	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,e_i)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   248	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a line that
   249	  goes through $u$ and is parallel to a uniformly random axis $i \in
   250	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   251	\end{lemma}
   252	\begin{proof}
   253		Since $s$ is uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $m$ divides $q$ by assumption, we
   254	  have that $i$ is uniformly random between $\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ and therefore
   255	  $(u_0,s)$ specifies a uniformly random axis-parallel line $\line(u_0,e_i)$.
   256	  Since $u_0 = L^{\lnf}_{e_i}(u)$, we have that $u \in \line(u_0,e_i)$.
   257	\end{proof}
   258	
   259	
   260	
   261	\begin{lemma}
   262		\label{lem:dlnf}
   263		Consider the pair $(\line,u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   264	  tuple $((u_0,s,v),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$,
   265	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,v)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   266	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a random
   267	  diagonal line that goes through $u$ and shares the first $i-1$ coordinates
   268	  with $u$, for uniformly random $i$.
   269	\end{lemma}
   270	\begin{proof}
   271		The proof of this follows identically to \Cref{lem:alnf}.
   272	\end{proof}
   273	
   274	For later convenience we make the following definition. 
   275	
   276	\begin{definition}[Line-point distributions]
   277	        \label{def:line-point-dist}
   278	 The \emph{axis line-point distribution} $D_{\ALine}$ is the
   279	 distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$ over pairs $(\ell=(u_0,e_i),u)$
   280	 (we omit the $0$ elements for simplicity). The \emph{diagonal
   281	   line-point distribution} $D_{\DLine}$ is the distribution
   282	 $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$  over $(\ell=(u_0,s,v),u)$. The
   283	 \emph{line-point distribution} $D_{\Line}$ is the equal mixture of the axis-parallel line-point distribution and the diagonal line-point distribution.
   284	 In other words, a sample from $D_{\Line}$ is distributed as follows:
   285	 with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$, output a sample from $D_{\ALine}$,
   286	 and with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$, output a sample from $D_{\DLine}$.
   287	\end{definition}

   320	\paragraph{Decision procedure} The decision procedure $\decider^\ld$ for the
   321	game $\game^\ld$ is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}.
   322	The table at the top specifies a parsing scheme for the questions and answers,
   323	depending on the type of question.
   324	For example, when a player receives a question with type $\Point$, the question
   325	content $x$, a bit string of length $m \log q$, should be interpreted by the
   326	decision procedure and the players as an element of the vector space $\F_q^m$,
   327	as indicated in Section~\ref{sec:ff-representations}.
   328	Similarly the answer to a question with type $\Point$ is expected to be a bit
   329	string of length $\ldc \log q$, and is interpreted as an element of $\F_q^\ldc$.
   330	For questions with type $\ALine$, the question content is a $(m \log q + \log
   331	q)$-bit string, which is parsed as a pair $(u_0, s) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q$,
   332	which in turn can be interpreted as a specification for an axis-parallel line
   333	$\line(u_0,e_i)$ in $\F_q^m$ where $i = \chi(s)$, as described in
   334	\Cref{lem:alnf}.
   335	The answer is interpreted as the description of $\ldc$ degree-$d$ univariate
   336	polynomials defined on the line $\line(u_0,e_i)$, each polynomial given by a
   337	list of $d+1$ coefficients.
   338	For questions with type $\DLine$, the question content is a $(2m \log q + \log
   339	q)$-bit string, which is parsed as a triple $(u_0, s, v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q
   340	\times \F_q^m$ that specifies a diagonal line $\line(u_0,v')$ where $v' =
   341	\pi_{i-1}(v)$ as described in \Cref{lem:dlnf}.
   342	The answer is interpreted as the description of $\ldc$ degree-$md$ univariate
   343	polynomials defined on the line $\line(u_0,v')$.
   344	If the answers returned by the players do not fit this format the decision
   345	procedure rejects.
   346	
   347	
   348	\begin{figure}[!htbp]
   349	  \centering
   350	  \begin{gamespec}
   351	    \setlength{\tabcolsep}{1em}
   352	    \begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{ l   l   X   }
   353	      \toprule
   354	      Type & Question Content & Answer Format \\
   355	      \midrule
   356	      $\Point$ & $ u \in \F_q^m$ & Element of $\F_q^\ldc$  \\
   357	      $\ALine$ & $ (u_0, s) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q$ &
   358	      $\ldc$ degree-$d$ polynomials $f_j: \F_q \to \F_q$\\
   359	      $\DLine$ & $(u_0, s, v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q \times \F_q^m$ & 
   360	      $\ldc$ degree-$md$ polynomials $f_j: \F_q \to \F_q$\\
   361	      \bottomrule
   362	    \end{tabularx}
   363	
   364	    \vspace{1em}
   365	
   366	    Input to $\decider^\ld$: $(\tvar_\alice,x_\alice, \tvar_\bob, x_\bob,
   367	    a_\alice, a_\bob)$.
   368	    In all cases where no action is indicated, accept.
   369	    For $w \in \AB$,
   370	
   371	    \begin{enumerate}
   372	      \setlength\itemsep{1pt}
   373	    \item (\textbf{Consistency test}) If $\tvar_\alice = \tvar_\bob$, accept iff
   374	      $a_\alice = a_\bob$.
   375	    \item (\textbf{Axis-parallel line-versus-point test}) If $\tvar_w = \ALine$
   376	      and $\tvar_{\overline{w}} = \Point$, accept iff $f_j(t) =
   377	      (a_{\overline{w}})_j$ for all $j \in \{1,2,\ldots,\ldc\}$ where $t \in
   378	      \F_q$ is such that $x_{\overline{w}} = u_0 + te_i$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   379	      
   380	    \item (\textbf{Diagonal line-versus-point test}) If $\tvar_w = \DLine$ and
   381	      $\tvar_{\overline{w}} = \Point$, accept iff $f_j(t) =
   382	      (a_{\overline{w}})_j$ for all $j \in \{1,2,\ldots,\ldc\}$ where $t \in
   383	      \F_q$ is such that $x_{\overline{w}} = u_0 + tv'$, where $v' =
   384	      \pi_{i-1}(v)$ with $i = \chi(s)$.
   385	    \end{enumerate}
   386	  \end{gamespec}
   387	  \caption{The decision procedure $\decider^\ld$ for the simultaneous low-degree
   388	    test, parameterized by $\ldparams = (q,m,d,\ldc)$.
   389	    The function $\chi(s)$ is defined in \Cref{eq:chi-func}, and $\pi_{i-1}(v)$
   390	    zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of $v$.}
   391	  \label{fig:ld-decider}
   392	\end{figure}
   393	
   394	We define a special class of measurements that are relevant to the soundness
   395	properties of the low-degree test.
   396	
   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.
   402	  More generally, for an integer $\ldc$ and tuples $m=(m_1, m_2, \ldots,
   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree). 
   408	\end{definition}
   409	
   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test. For our construction we use the low individual degree test, whose quantum soundness is shown in~\cite{ML20} and generalized in~\cite{ji2021quantum}. We state the result in the form that is most directly useful for us, and show how the stated result follows from~\cite{ji2021quantum}.

 private def CondLinearTerm.raiseLevel {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
     [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
     (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1) :=

 @[simp]
 private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_raiseLevel {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
     [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
     (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) (x : ι → K) :
     CondLinearTerm.eval t.raiseLevel x = CondLinearTerm.eval t x := by
   simp [CondLinearTerm.raiseLevel, CondLinearTerm.eval]
 
 private theorem CondLinearTerm.raiseLevel_supportedOn {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
     [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
     {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell} {S : Finset ι}
     (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) :
     CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t.raiseLevel S := by
   exact ⟨Finset.empty_subset S, fun _ => by simpa using ht⟩

-number of empty stages. -/
+number of levels, each with zero linear contribution. -/
 private def CondLinearTerm.raiseBy {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
     [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :
     (d : ℕ) → {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell →
       CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + d)
   | 0, _, t => t
   | d + 1, _, t => (raiseBy d t).raiseLevel
 
 @[simp]
 private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_raiseBy {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
     [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (d : ℕ) {ell : ℕ}
     (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) (x : ι → K) :
     CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.raiseBy d t) x = CondLinearTerm.eval t x := by
   induction d with
   | zero => rfl
   | succ d ih => simp [CondLinearTerm.raiseBy, ih]
 
 private theorem CondLinearTerm.raiseBy_supportedOn {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
     [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (d : ℕ) {ell : ℕ}
     {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell} {S : Finset ι}
     (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) :
     CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (CondLinearTerm.raiseBy d t) S := by
   induction d with
   | zero => exact ht
   | succ d ih => exact CondLinearTerm.raiseLevel_supportedOn ih
 
 /-- Conditional linearity is monotone in the number of levels. -/
 private theorem IsCondLinearOn.mono_level {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
     [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {S : Finset ι} {ell k : ℕ}
     {L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)} (hL : IsCondLinearOn K S ell L)
     (h : ell ≤ k) : IsCondLinearOn K S k L := by
   rcases hL with ⟨t, ht, ht_eval⟩
   have hk : ell + (k - ell) = k := Nat.add_sub_of_le h
   rw [← hk]
   exact ⟨CondLinearTerm.raiseBy (k - ell) t,
     CondLinearTerm.raiseBy_supportedOn _ ht,
     funext fun x => by rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_raiseBy, congrFun ht_eval x]⟩
 
 /-- A conditionally-linear map supported on `S` has values supported on `S`. -/
 private theorem IsCondLinearOn.apply_eq_zero_of_not_mem {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
     [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {S : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
     {L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)} (hL : IsCondLinearOn K S ell L)
     (x : ι → K) {a : ι} (ha : a ∉ S) : L x a = 0 := by
   rcases hL with ⟨t, ht, ht_eval⟩
   rw [← congrFun (congrFun ht_eval x) a]
   exact CondLinearTerm.eval_eq_zero_of_not_mem ht x ha
 
 /-- A conditionally-linear map supported on `S` depends only on the input in

 private theorem IsCondLinearOn.apply_coordinateRestriction {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
     [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {S : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
     {L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)} (hL : IsCondLinearOn K S ell L)
     (x : ι → K) : L (coordinateRestriction S x) = L x := by
   rcases hL with ⟨t, ht, ht_eval⟩
   rw [← congrFun ht_eval, CondLinearTerm.eval_coordinateRestriction ht,
     congrFun ht_eval]

+/-- Prepend a first-level linear contribution, supported on one register, to a
+family of residual conditionally linear maps indexed by its value. -/
 private theorem IsCondLinearOn.cons {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
     [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {S S₁ : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
     (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
     (hS₁ : S₁ ⊆ S) (hSupport : ∀ x a, a ∉ S₁ → L₁ x a = 0)
     (R : (ι → K) → (ι → K) → (ι → K))
     (hR : ∀ y, IsCondLinearOn K (S \ S₁) ell (R y)) :
     IsCondLinearOn K S (ell + 1) (fun x =>
       L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x) +
         R (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x)) x) := by
   classical
   choose t ht ht_eval using hR
   refine ⟨.succ S₁ L₁ hSupport t, ⟨hS₁, ht⟩, ?_⟩
   funext x
   change L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x) +
       CondLinearTerm.eval (t (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x))) x = _
   rw [congrFun (ht_eval _) x]
 
 private theorem coordinateRestriction_eq_self {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
     [DecidableEq ι] {S : Finset ι} {x : ι → K}
     (hx : ∀ a, a ∉ S → x a = 0) : coordinateRestriction S x = x := by
   ext a
   by_cases ha : a ∈ S
   · simp [coordinateRestriction, ha]
   · simp [coordinateRestriction, ha, hx a ha]
 
 private theorem coordinateRestriction_add {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
     [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) (x y : ι → K) :
     coordinateRestriction S (x + y) =
       coordinateRestriction S x + coordinateRestriction S y := by
   ext a

 \begin{definition}[Graph distribution]\label{def:graph-distribution}
 	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.graphDistribution}
 	\leanok
 	Let $G = (U, E)$ be an undirected graph with vertex set $U$ and nonempty edge set $E$. Edges in $E$ are written as multisets $\{u, v\}$ of two vertices; the case $u = v$ represents a self-loop. Suppose there are $m \ge 1$ edges, $k$ of which are self-loops. Then the \emph{graph distribution $\mu_G$ of $G$} is the distribution over $U \times U$ such that for every $(u,v) \in U \times U$,
 	\[
 		\mu_G(u, v) =
 		\begin{cases}
 			1/(2m-k) & \text{if } \{u,v\} \in E\,,\\
 			0 & \text{otherwise}\,.
 		\end{cases}
 	\]
 	This is identical to the uniform distribution over ordered pairs $(u,v) \in U \times U$ such that $\{u,v\} \in E$: each edge that is not a self-loop contributes two ordered pairs, and each self-loop contributes one, whence the normalization $2m-k$.
 \end{definition}

 \end{lemma}
 \begin{proof}

     9	This file introduces the finite question and answer alphabets used by the
    10	low-degree component of the Pauli basis test.  The maps are explicit maps on
    11	the ambient coefficient space, and their conditional-linearity levels are
    12	established below; the line-point distributions they induce are analysed in
    13	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/LowDegreeGameTheorems.lean`.
    14	
    15	## References
    16	
    17	The source-facing nodes are `def:ld-game`, `def:ld-question-distribution`, and
    18	`def:ld-win-predicate` in
    19	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-156`; their paper origin is
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    21	-/
    22

    24	
    25	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT

    31	/-- Numerical parameters for the low-degree game.  The ambient coefficient
    32	space uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq`, rather than a
    33	model supplied by each parameter record.  This is the Lean carrier for
    34	`def:ld-game` in
    35	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-156`, with paper origin
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    37	-/
    38	structure LdParams where
    39	  q : ℕ
    40	  m : ℕ
    41	  d : ℕ
    42	  k : ℕ
    43	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    44	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    45	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    46	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    47	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    48	
    49	/-- The positive dimension in `LdParams` supplies the finite coordinate type
    50	used by the uniform axis and prefix-index marginals. -/
    51	instance (L : LdParams) : Nonempty (Fin L.m) :=
    52	  ⟨⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one L.hm⟩⟩
    53	
    54	/-- The fixed model accessor for an `LdParams` record.  It is a compatibility
    55	view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently quantified
    56	parameter.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`; paper origin
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    58	-/
    59	noncomputable def LdParams.model (P : LdParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
    60	  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq
    61	
    62	/-- The scalar carrier selected by an `LdParams` record; this is the fixed
    63	field carrier in `def:ld-game`, selected globally by `LdParams.model`.
    64	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`, paper origin
    65	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    66	-/
    67	abbrev ScalarQ (P : LdParams) := (P.model).K
    68	
    69	/-- The three low-degree question types of `def:ld-game`, blueprint
    70	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`, paper origin
    71	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    72	-/
    73	inductive LdType where
    74	  | point
    75	  | aline
    76	  | dline
    77	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    78	
    79	/-- The register index used by the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    80	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`; paper origin
    81	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    82	-/
    83	abbrev LdIndex (P : LdParams) := (Fin P.m ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m
    84	
    85	/-- The full ambient low-degree coefficient space (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    86	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`; paper origin
    87	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    88	-/
    89	abbrev LdSpace (P : LdParams) := LdIndex P → ScalarQ P
    90	
    91	/-- The point coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    92	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    93	-/
    94	def LdSpace.point {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    95	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))
    96	
    97	/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
    98	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    99	-/
   100	def LdSpace.seed {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=
   101	  z (.inl (.inr ()) )
   102	
   103	/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
   104	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   105	-/
   106	def LdSpace.direction {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   107	  fun i => z (.inr i)
   108	
   109	/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
   110	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   111	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   112	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   113	-/
   114	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   115	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   116	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   117	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   118	
   119	/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the
   120	chosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector.  This is the
   121	prefix restriction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   122	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   124	-/
   125	def prefixProjection {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   126	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   127	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   128	
   129	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   130	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   131	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   132	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   133	-/
   134	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   135	  fun i => match i with
   136	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   137	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   138	  | .inr _ => 0
   139	
   140	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   141	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   142	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper
   143	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   144	-/
   145	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   146	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   147	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   148	  fun i => match i with
   149	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   150	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   151	  | .inr _ => 0
   152	
   153	/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
   154	for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   155	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   156	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper origin
   157	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   158	-/
   159	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   160	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   161	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   162	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   163	  fun i => match i with
   164	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   165	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   166	  | .inr j => direction j
   167	
   168	/-- Dispatch the three low-degree CL maps by question type.  This is the typed
   169	construction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   170	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   171	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   172	-/
   173	noncomputable def ldCL (P : LdParams) : LdType → LdSpace P → LdSpace P
   174	  | .point => ldPointCL P
   175	  | .aline => ldALineCL P
   176	  | .dline => ldDLineCL P
   177	
   178	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the register carrying the shared scalar
   179	coordinate of the ambient low-degree space.  It is the first register in the
   180	concatenation exhibiting the conditional-linearity levels asserted in
   181	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   182	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   183	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`. -/
   184	private def ldSeedRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=
   185	  {Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())}
   186	
   187	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the register carrying the point coordinates
   188	of the ambient low-degree space; see `ldSeedRegister`. -/
   189	private def ldPointRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=
   190	  Finset.univ.image fun j : Fin P.m => (Sum.inl (Sum.inl j) : LdIndex P)
   191	
   192	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the register carrying the direction
   193	coordinates of the ambient low-degree space; see `ldSeedRegister`. -/
   194	private def ldDirectionRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=
   195	  Finset.univ.image fun j : Fin P.m => (Sum.inr j : LdIndex P)
   196	
   197	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map retaining the shared scalar
   198	coordinate and clearing every other coordinate. -/
   199	private def ldSeedLinear (P : LdParams) :
   200	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   201	  toFun x := fun i =>
   202	    match i with
   203	    | .inl (.inl _) => 0
   204	    | .inl (.inr _) => x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))
   205	    | .inr _ => 0
   206	  map_add' x y := by
   207	    funext i
   208	    rcases i with (j | u) | j <;> simp
   209	  map_smul' c x := by
   210	    funext i
   211	    rcases i with (j | u) | j <;> simp
   212	
   213	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map sending the point block to its
   214	canonical line representative in the fixed direction `v` and clearing every
   215	other coordinate. -/
   216	private noncomputable def ldPointCLLinear (P : LdParams) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   217	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   218	  toFun x := fun i =>
   219	    match i with
   220	    | .inl (.inl j) => lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point x) j
   221	    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   222	    | .inr _ => 0
   223	  map_add' x y := by
   224	    funext i
   225	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
   226	    · change lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point (x + y)) j = _
   227	      have hpoint : LdSpace.point (x + y) = LdSpace.point x + LdSpace.point y := rfl
   228	      rw [hpoint, map_add]
   229	      rfl
   230	    · simp
   231	    · simp
   232	  map_smul' c x := by
   233	    funext i
   234	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
   235	    · change lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point (c • x)) j = _
   236	      have hpoint : LdSpace.point (c • x) = c • LdSpace.point x := rfl
   237	      rw [hpoint, map_smul]
   238	      rfl
   239	    · simp
   240	    · simp
   241	
   242	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map zeroing the first `i`
   243	coordinates of the direction block and clearing every other coordinate. -/
   244	private def ldDirectionCLLinear (P : LdParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
   245	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   246	  toFun x := fun k =>
   247	    match k with
   248	    | .inl (.inl _) => 0
   249	    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   250	    | .inr j => prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction x) j
   251	  map_add' x y := by
   252	    funext k
   253	    rcases k with (j | u) | j
   254	    · simp
   255	    · simp
   256	    · change prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction (x + y)) j =
   257	        prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction x) j +
   258	          prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction y) j
   259	      by_cases h : j.val < i.val
   260	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_pos h, add_zero]
   261	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_neg h]
   262	        rfl
   263	  map_smul' c x := by
   264	    funext k
   265	    rcases k with (j | u) | j
   266	    · simp
   267	    · simp
   268	    · change prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction (c • x)) j =
   269	        c • prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction x) j
   270	      by_cases h : j.val < i.val
   271	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_pos h, smul_zero]
   272	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_neg h]
   273	        rfl
   274	
   275	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the shared-scalar map vanishes
   276	outside the scalar register. -/
   277	private theorem ldSeedLinear_supported (P : LdParams) :
   278	    ∀ (x : LdSpace P) (i : LdIndex P), i ∉ ldSeedRegister P →
   279	      ldSeedLinear P x i = 0 := by
   280	  intro x i hi
   281	  rcases i with (j | u) | j
   282	  · rfl
   283	  · cases u
   284	    exact absurd (Finset.mem_singleton_self _) hi
   285	  · rfl
   286	
   287	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the canonical-representative map
   288	vanishes outside the point register. -/
   289	private theorem ldPointCLLinear_supported (P : LdParams) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   290	    ∀ (x : LdSpace P) (i : LdIndex P), i ∉ ldPointRegister P →
   291	      ldPointCLLinear P v x i = 0 := by
   292	  intro x i hi
   293	  rcases i with (j | u) | j
   294	  · exact absurd (Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ (Finset.mem_univ j)) hi
   295	  · rfl
   296	  · rfl
   297	
   298	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the prefix-zeroing map vanishes
   299	outside the direction register. -/
   300	private theorem ldDirectionCLLinear_supported (P : LdParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
   301	    ∀ (x : LdSpace P) (k : LdIndex P), k ∉ ldDirectionRegister P →
   302	      ldDirectionCLLinear P i x k = 0 := by
   303	  intro x k hk
   304	  rcases k with (j | u) | j
   305	  · rfl
   306	  · rfl
   307	  · exact absurd (Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ (Finset.mem_univ j)) hk
   308	
   309	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the point register is disjoint from
   310	the scalar register. -/
   311	private theorem ldPointRegister_subset_sdiff_seed (P : LdParams) :
   312	    ldPointRegister P ⊆ Finset.univ \ ldSeedRegister P := by
   313	  intro i hi
   314	  obtain ⟨j, -, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hi
   315	  simp [ldSeedRegister]
   316	
   317	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the direction register is disjoint
   318	from the scalar register. -/
   319	private theorem ldDirectionRegister_subset_sdiff_seed (P : LdParams) :
   320	    ldDirectionRegister P ⊆ Finset.univ \ ldSeedRegister P := by
   321	  intro i hi
   322	  obtain ⟨j, -, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hi
   323	  simp [ldSeedRegister]
   324	
   325	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the point register is disjoint from
   326	both the scalar and the direction registers. -/
   327	private theorem ldPointRegister_subset_sdiff_seed_direction (P : LdParams) :
   328	    ldPointRegister P ⊆
   329	      (Finset.univ \ ldSeedRegister P) \ ldDirectionRegister P := by
   330	  intro i hi
   331	  obtain ⟨j, -, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hi
   332	  simp [ldSeedRegister, ldDirectionRegister]
   333	
   334	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: restricting to the scalar register
   335	leaves the shared scalar coordinate unchanged. -/
   336	private theorem coordinateRestriction_seed (P : LdParams) (x : LdSpace P) :
   337	    coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())) =
   338	      x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())) := by
   339	  have hmem : (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()) : LdIndex P) ∈ ldSeedRegister P :=
   340	    Finset.mem_singleton_self _
   341	  simp [coordinateRestriction, hmem]
   342	
   343	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: restricting to the point register
   344	leaves the point block unchanged. -/
   345	private theorem coordinateRestriction_point (P : LdParams) (x : LdSpace P) :
   346	    LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) = LdSpace.point x := by
   347	  funext j
   348	  have hmem : (Sum.inl (Sum.inl j) : LdIndex P) ∈ ldPointRegister P :=
   349	    Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ (Finset.mem_univ j)
   350	  simp [LdSpace.point, coordinateRestriction, hmem]
   351	
   352	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: restricting to the direction register
   353	leaves the direction block unchanged. -/
   354	private theorem coordinateRestriction_direction (P : LdParams) (x : LdSpace P) :
   355	    LdSpace.direction (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x) =
   356	      LdSpace.direction x := by
   357	  funext j
   358	  have hmem : (Sum.inr j : LdIndex P) ∈ ldDirectionRegister P :=
   359	    Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ (Finset.mem_univ j)
   360	  simp [LdSpace.direction, coordinateRestriction, hmem]
   361	
   362	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: a two-level representation of the
   363	affine-line map as a conditionally linear function. -/
   364	private noncomputable def ldALineTerm (P : LdParams) :
   365	    CondLinearTerm (ScalarQ P) (ι := LdIndex P) 2 :=
   366	  .succ (ldSeedRegister P) (ldSeedLinear P) (ldSeedLinear_supported P)
   367	    fun y =>
   368	      .succ (ldPointRegister P)
   369	        (ldPointCLLinear P (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed y))))
   370	        (ldPointCLLinear_supported P _)
   371	        fun _ => .zero
   372	
   373	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: a three-level representation of the
   374	diagonal-line map as a conditionally linear function. -/
   375	private noncomputable def ldDLineTerm (P : LdParams) :
   376	    CondLinearTerm (ScalarQ P) (ι := LdIndex P) 3 :=
   377	  .succ (ldSeedRegister P) (ldSeedLinear P) (ldSeedLinear_supported P)
   378	    fun y =>
   379	      .succ (ldDirectionRegister P)
   380	        (ldDirectionCLLinear P (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed y)))

381	        (ldDirectionCLLinear_supported P _)
   382	        fun w =>
   383	          .succ (ldPointRegister P)
   384	            (ldPointCLLinear P (LdSpace.direction w))
   385	            (ldPointCLLinear_supported P _)
   386	            fun _ => .zero
   387	
   388	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the affine-line map.  This is
   389	`lem:ld-aline-level`, the level-2 assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`;
   390	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:61-71`, paper
   391	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   392	-/
   393	theorem isCondLinear_ldALineCL (P : LdParams) :
   394	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 2 (ldALineCL P) := by
   395	  refine ⟨ldALineTerm P, ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, fun _ =>
   396	    ⟨ldPointRegister_subset_sdiff_seed P, fun _ => trivial⟩⟩, ?_⟩
   397	  funext x
   398	  have hseed :
   399	      LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x)) =
   400	        LdSpace.seed x := coordinateRestriction_seed P x
   401	  have hpoint : LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) =
   402	      LdSpace.point x := coordinateRestriction_point P x
   403	  have hval :
   404	      CondLinearTerm.eval (ldALineTerm P) x =
   405	        ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   406	          (ldPointCLLinear P (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))
   407	            (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0) := by
   408	    change ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   409	        (ldPointCLLinear P
   410	            (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P
   411	              (LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x)))))
   412	            (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0) = _
   413	    rw [hseed]
   414	  rw [hval]
   415	  funext i
   416	  rcases i with (j | u) | j
   417	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) +
   418	        (lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))
   419	          (LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x)) j + 0) =
   420	      lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))
   421	        (LdSpace.point x) j
   422	    rw [hpoint, zero_add, add_zero]
   423	  · change coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())) +
   424	        ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0) = x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))
   425	    rw [coordinateRestriction_seed, add_zero, add_zero]
   426	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) + ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0) = 0
   427	    rw [add_zero, add_zero]
   428	
   429	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the diagonal-line map.  This is
   430	`lem:ld-dline-level`, the level-3 assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`;
   431	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:73-83`, paper origin
   432	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   433	-/
   434	theorem isCondLinear_ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) :
   435	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 3 (ldDLineCL P) := by
   436	  refine ⟨ldDLineTerm P, ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, fun _ =>
   437	    ⟨ldDirectionRegister_subset_sdiff_seed P, fun _ =>
   438	      ⟨ldPointRegister_subset_sdiff_seed_direction P, fun _ => trivial⟩⟩⟩, ?_⟩
   439	  funext x
   440	  have hseed :
   441	      LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x)) =
   442	        LdSpace.seed x := coordinateRestriction_seed P x
   443	  have hpoint : LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) =
   444	      LdSpace.point x := coordinateRestriction_point P x
   445	  have hdir :
   446	      LdSpace.direction
   447	          (ldDirectionCLLinear P (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
   448	            (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)) =
   449	        prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x) := by
   450	    funext j
   451	    change prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
   452	        (LdSpace.direction (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)) j = _
   453	    rw [coordinateRestriction_direction]
   454	  have hval :
   455	      CondLinearTerm.eval (ldDLineTerm P) x =
   456	        ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   457	          (ldDirectionCLLinear P (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
   458	              (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x) +
   459	            (ldPointCLLinear P
   460	                (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x))
   461	                (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0)) := by
   462	    change ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   463	        (ldDirectionCLLinear P
   464	            (chiIndex P
   465	              (LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x))))
   466	            (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x) +
   467	          (ldPointCLLinear P
   468	              (LdSpace.direction
   469	                (ldDirectionCLLinear P
   470	                  (chiIndex P
   471	                    (LdSpace.seed
   472	                      (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x))))
   473	                  (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)))
   474	              (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0)) = _
   475	    rw [hseed, hdir]
   476	  rw [hval]
   477	  funext i
   478	  rcases i with (j | u) | j
   479	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) + ((0 : ScalarQ P) +
   480	        (lineRepMap
   481	          (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x))
   482	          (LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x)) j + 0)) =
   483	      lineRepMap (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x))
   484	        (LdSpace.point x) j
   485	    rw [hpoint, zero_add, zero_add, add_zero]
   486	  · change coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())) +
   487	        ((0 : ScalarQ P) + ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0)) = x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))
   488	    rw [coordinateRestriction_seed, add_zero, add_zero, add_zero]
   489	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) +
   490	        (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
   491	            (LdSpace.direction (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)) j +
   492	          ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0)) =
   493	      prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x) j
   494	    rw [coordinateRestriction_direction, zero_add, add_zero, add_zero]

   496	/-- The question alphabet for the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
   497	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`; paper origin
   498	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   499	-/
   500	abbrev LdQuestion (P : LdParams) := LdType × LdSpace P
   501	
   502	/-- The typed CL question distribution.  This is the inlined construction in
   503	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper
   504	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   505	-/
   506	noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :
   507	    Distribution (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   508	  Distribution.map
   509	    (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P))
   510	    (fun s =>
   511	      ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   512	
   513	/-- The coefficient-tuple answer alphabet of the low-degree game.  Polynomial
   514	answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in
   515	the paper, as required by `def:ld-win-predicate` (blueprint
   516	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`; paper
   517	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   518	-/
   519	inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
   520	  | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)
   521	  | alinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   522	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   523	  deriving DecidableEq
   524	
   525	/-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`
   526	instance; the public constructors are those of `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   527	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
   528	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   529	-/
   530	abbrev LdAnswerCode (P : LdParams) :=
   531	  (Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   532	    ((Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   533	      (Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P))
   534	
   535	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `LdAnswer` (Lean-only
   536	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   537	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
   538	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   539	-/
   540	noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
   541	    LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where
   542	  toFun
   543	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   544	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   545	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   546	  invFun
   547	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   548	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   549	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   550	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   551	  right_inv := by
   552	    intro x
   553	    cases x with
   554	    | inl a => rfl
   555	    | inr x =>
   556	        cases x with
   557	        | inl a => rfl
   558	        | inr a => rfl
   559	
   560	instance (P : LdParams) : Inhabited (LdAnswer P) :=
   561	  ⟨.pointVals (fun _ => 0)⟩
   562	
   563	noncomputable instance (P : LdParams) : Fintype (LdAnswer P) :=
   564	  Fintype.ofEquiv (LdAnswerCode P) (ldAnswerEquiv P).symm
   565	
   566	/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
   567	representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   568	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
   569	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   570	-/
   571	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
   572	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
   573	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
   574	
   575	/-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
   576	Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   577	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
   578	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   579	-/
   580	def validLdAnswer {P : LdParams} (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
   581	  match t, a with
   582	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   583	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   584	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   585	  | _, _ => false
   586	
   587	/-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   588	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
   589	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   590	-/
   591	def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   592	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   593	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   594	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   595	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   596	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   597	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   598	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   599	
   600	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   601	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
   602	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   603	-/
   604	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   605	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   606	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   607	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   608	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   609	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   610	
   611	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   612	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   613	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
   614	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   615	-/
   616	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   617	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   618	  open Classical in
   619	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   620	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   621	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   622	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   623	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   624	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   625	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   626	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   627	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   628	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   629	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   630	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   631	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   632	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   633	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   634	      else false
   635	
   636	/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
   637	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-156`, paper origin
   638	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   639	-/
   640	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   641	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   642	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   643	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   644	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   645	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   646	  μ_prob := by
   647	    exact Distribution.IsProbability.map
   648	      (uniformDistribution_isProbability ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P)) _
   649	  decide := ldWinPredicate P
   650	
   651	end

    36	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary equivalence splitting an ambient low-degree
    37	vector into its point, seed, and direction blocks. -/
    38	private def ldSpaceSplit (L : LdParams) :
    39	    LdSpace L ≃ ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) where
    40	  toFun z := ((LdSpace.point z, LdSpace.seed z), LdSpace.direction z)
    41	  invFun p := fun i =>
    42	    match i with
    43	    | .inl (.inl j) => p.1.1 j
    44	    | .inl (.inr _) => p.1.2
    45	    | .inr j => p.2 j
    46	  left_inv z := by
    47	    funext i
    48	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
    49	    · rfl
    50	    · cases u
    51	      rfl
    52	    · rfl
    53	  right_inv p := by
    54	    obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, c⟩ := p
    55	    rfl

    68	            Prod.fst).map Prod.fst := by

    71	    _ = ((uniformDistribution

   113	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: every fiber of the coordinate index has
   114	exactly `q / m` elements.  This is the balance property used in
   115	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`. -/
   117	private theorem card_chiIndex_fiber (L : LdParams) (i : Fin L.m) :
   118	    ((Finset.univ : Finset (ScalarQ L)).filter fun s => chiIndex L s = i).card
   119	      = L.q / L.m := by
   120	  have hq : 0 < L.q := ldParams_q_pos L
   121	  have hqk : L.m * (L.q / L.m) = L.q := Nat.mul_div_cancel' L.hdvd
   122	  have hkpos : 0 < L.q / L.m := by
   123	    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (L.q / L.m) with h | h
   124	    · rw [h, Nat.mul_zero] at hqk
   125	      omega
   126	    · exact h
   127	  have hstep1 :
   128	      ((Finset.univ : Finset (ScalarQ L)).filter fun s => chiIndex L s = i).card
   129	        = ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
   130	            fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val).card := by
   131	    refine Finset.card_equiv (binaryRepresentation L.model) fun s => ?_
   132	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, chiIndex_eq_iff]
   133	  have hstep2 :
   134	      ((Finset.range L.q).filter fun t => (t / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val)
   135	        = ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
   136	            fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val).image Fin.val := by
   137	    ext t
   138	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_range, Finset.mem_image,
   139	      Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
   140	    constructor
   141	    · rintro ⟨ht, hP⟩
   142	      exact ⟨⟨t, ht⟩, hP, rfl⟩
   143	    · rintro ⟨n, hP, rfl⟩
   144	      exact ⟨n.isLt, hP⟩
   145	  have hstep3 :
   146	      ((Finset.range L.q).filter fun t => (t / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val)
   147	        = Finset.Ico (i.val * (L.q / L.m)) (i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m) := by
   148	    ext t
   149	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_range, Finset.mem_Ico]
   150	    constructor
   151	    · rintro ⟨htq, hP⟩
   152	      have hlt : t / (L.q / L.m) < L.m := by
   153	        rw [Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos]
   154	        omega
   155	      have hdiv : t / (L.q / L.m) = i.val := by
   156	        rwa [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hlt] at hP
   157	      have hle : t / (L.q / L.m) * (L.q / L.m) ≤ t := Nat.div_mul_le_self t _
   158	      have hupper : t < (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m) := by
   159	        rw [← Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos, hdiv]
   160	        omega
   161	      have hexp : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m)
   162	          = i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m := by ring
   163	      rw [hdiv] at hle
   164	      omega
   165	    · rintro ⟨hlo, hhi⟩
   166	      have hexp : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m)
   167	          = i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m := by ring
   168	      have hdiv : t / (L.q / L.m) = i.val := by
   169	        have h1 : i.val ≤ t / (L.q / L.m) := (Nat.le_div_iff_mul_le hkpos).mpr hlo
   170	        have h2 : t / (L.q / L.m) < i.val + 1 := by
   171	          rw [Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos]
   172	          omega
   173	        omega
   174	      refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
   175	      · have hbound : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m) ≤ L.m * (L.q / L.m) :=
   176	          Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ i.isLt
   177	        omega
   178	      · rw [hdiv, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt i.isLt]
   179	  rw [hstep1, ← Finset.card_image_of_injective
   180	      ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
   181	        fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val) Fin.val_injective,
   182	    ← hstep2, hstep3, Nat.card_Ico]
   183	  omega

   189	private theorem map_uniformDistribution_chiIndex (L : LdParams) :

   194	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: zeroing an initial segment of the

   196	private theorem prefixProjection_prefixProjection (L : LdParams) (i : Fin L.m)
   197	    (v : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) :

   118	    ((Finset.univ : Finset (ScalarQ L)).filter fun s => chiIndex L s = i).card
   119	      = L.q / L.m := by
   120	  have hq : 0 < L.q := ldParams_q_pos L
   121	  have hqk : L.m * (L.q / L.m) = L.q := Nat.mul_div_cancel' L.hdvd
   122	  have hkpos : 0 < L.q / L.m := by
   123	    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (L.q / L.m) with h | h
   124	    · rw [h, Nat.mul_zero] at hqk
   125	      omega
   126	    · exact h
   127	  have hstep1 :
   128	      ((Finset.univ : Finset (ScalarQ L)).filter fun s => chiIndex L s = i).card
   129	        = ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
   130	            fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val).card := by
   131	    refine Finset.card_equiv (binaryRepresentation L.model) fun s => ?_
   132	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, chiIndex_eq_iff]

   134	      ((Finset.range L.q).filter fun t => (t / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val)
   135	        = ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
   136	            fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val).image Fin.val := by
   137	    ext t
   138	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_range, Finset.mem_image,
   139	      Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
   140	    constructor
   141	    · rintro ⟨ht, hP⟩
   142	      exact ⟨⟨t, ht⟩, hP, rfl⟩
   143	    · rintro ⟨n, hP, rfl⟩
   144	      exact ⟨n.isLt, hP⟩
   145	  have hstep3 :
   146	      ((Finset.range L.q).filter fun t => (t / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val)
   147	        = Finset.Ico (i.val * (L.q / L.m)) (i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m) := by
   148	    ext t
   149	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_range, Finset.mem_Ico]
   150	    constructor
   151	    · rintro ⟨htq, hP⟩
   152	      have hlt : t / (L.q / L.m) < L.m := by
   153	        rw [Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos]
   154	        omega
   155	      have hdiv : t / (L.q / L.m) = i.val := by
   156	        rwa [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hlt] at hP
   157	      have hle : t / (L.q / L.m) * (L.q / L.m) ≤ t := Nat.div_mul_le_self t _
   158	      have hupper : t < (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m) := by
   159	        rw [← Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos, hdiv]
   160	        omega
   161	      have hexp : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m)
   162	          = i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m := by ring
   163	      rw [hdiv] at hle
   164	      omega
   165	    · rintro ⟨hlo, hhi⟩
   166	      have hexp : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m)
   167	          = i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m := by ring
   168	      have hdiv : t / (L.q / L.m) = i.val := by
   169	        have h1 : i.val ≤ t / (L.q / L.m) := (Nat.le_div_iff_mul_le hkpos).mpr hlo
   170	        have h2 : t / (L.q / L.m) < i.val + 1 := by
   171	          rw [Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos]
   172	          omega
   173	        omega
   174	      refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
   175	      · have hbound : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m) ≤ L.m * (L.q / L.m) :=
   176	          Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ i.isLt
   177	        omega
   178	      · rw [hdiv, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt i.isLt]
   179	  rw [hstep1, ← Finset.card_image_of_injective
   180	      ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
   181	        fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val) Fin.val_injective,

    21	noncomputable def Distribution.prod {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    22	    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β) : Distribution (α × β) where
    23	  support := μ.support.product ν.support
    24	  weight p := μ.weight p.1 * ν.weight p.2
    25	  nonnegative p := mul_nonneg (μ.nonnegative p.1) (ν.nonnegative p.2)
    26	  outsideSupport p hp := by
    27	    by_cases hμ : p.1 ∈ μ.support
    28	    · have hν : p.2 ∉ ν.support := by
    29	        intro h
    30	        exact hp (Finset.mem_product.mpr ⟨hμ, h⟩)
    31	      simp [ν.outsideSupport p.2 hν]
    32	    · simp [μ.outsideSupport p.1 hμ]

    34	/-- The product of two probability distributions is a probability
    35	distribution; blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:454-480`, paper
    36	`06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-501`. -/
    37	theorem Distribution.prod_isProbability {α β : Type*}
    38	    [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β)
    39	    (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (hν : ν.IsProbability) :
    40	    (Distribution.prod μ ν).IsProbability := by
    41	  simp only [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.totalWeight,
    42	    Distribution.prod]
    43	  calc
    44	    (∑ p ∈ μ.support.product ν.support, μ.weight p.1 * ν.weight p.2) =
    45	        ∑ a ∈ μ.support, ∑ b ∈ ν.support, μ.weight a * ν.weight b := by
    46	      exact Finset.sum_product' μ.support ν.support
    47	        (fun a b => μ.weight a * ν.weight b)
    48	    _ =
    49	        ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * ∑ b ∈ ν.support, ν.weight b := by
    50	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    51	      intro a _
    52	      exact (Finset.mul_sum ν.support (fun b => ν.weight b) (μ.weight a)).symm
    53	    _ = ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a := by
    54	      rw [hν.weight_sum_eq_one]
    55	      simp
    56	    _ = 1 := hμ.weight_sum_eq_one

    60	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:125-135`, paper
    61	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`. -/
    62	noncomputable def Distribution.mix {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    63	    (t : ℝ) (ht0 : 0 ≤ t) (ht1 : t ≤ 1)
    64	    (μ ν : Distribution α) : Distribution α where
    65	  support := μ.support ∪ ν.support
    66	  weight a := t * μ.weight a + (1 - t) * ν.weight a
    67	  nonnegative a := by
    68	    exact add_nonneg
    69	      (mul_nonneg ht0 (μ.nonnegative a))
    70	      (mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr ht1) (ν.nonnegative a))
    71	  outsideSupport a ha := by
    72	    have hμ : a ∉ μ.support := fun h => ha (Finset.mem_union_left _ h)
    73	    have hν : a ∉ ν.support := fun h => ha (Finset.mem_union_right _ h)
    74	    simp [μ.outsideSupport a hμ, ν.outsideSupport a hν]

    76	/-- A convex mixture of probability distributions is a probability distribution;
    77	`def:line-point-dist`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:125-135`, paper
    78	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`. -/
    79	theorem Distribution.mix_isProbability {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    80	    (t : ℝ) (μ ν : Distribution α) (hμ : μ.IsProbability)
    81	    (hν : ν.IsProbability) (ht0 : 0 ≤ t) (ht1 : t ≤ 1) :
    82	    (Distribution.mix t ht0 ht1 μ ν).IsProbability := by
    83	  have hμ_union :
    84	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support, μ.weight a = 1 := by
    85	    apply hμ.weight_sum_eq_one_of_subset
    86	    intro a ha
    87	    exact Finset.mem_union_left ν.support ha
    88	  have hν_union :
    89	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support, ν.weight a = 1 := by
    90	    apply hν.weight_sum_eq_one_of_subset
    91	    intro a ha
    92	    exact Finset.mem_union_right μ.support ha
    93	  simp only [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.totalWeight,
    94	    Distribution.mix]
    95	  rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.mul_sum,
    96	    hμ_union, hν_union]
    97	  ring

    99	/-- The dependent bind of finite distributions used for typed question
   100	distributions, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1400-1404`, paper
   101	`07_types.tex:84-94`. -/
   102	noncomputable def Distribution.bind {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
   103	    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : α → Distribution β) : Distribution β where
   104	  support := μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support)
   105	  weight b := ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * (ν a).weight b
   106	  nonnegative b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => mul_nonneg (μ.nonnegative a) ((ν a).nonnegative b)
   107	  outsideSupport b hb := by
   108	    apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
   109	    intro a ha
   110	    have hnot : b ∉ (ν a).support := by
   111	      intro h
   112	      exact hb (Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨a, ha, h⟩)
   113	    simp [ν a |>.outsideSupport b hnot]

   115	/-- A dependent bind of probability distributions is a probability distribution;
   116	blueprint
   117	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1400-1404`, paper `07_types.tex:84-94`. -/
   118	theorem Distribution.bind_isProbability {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
   119	    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : α → Distribution β) (hμ : μ.IsProbability)
   120	    (hν : ∀ a ∈ μ.support, (ν a).IsProbability) :
   121	    (Distribution.bind μ ν).IsProbability := by
   122	  classical
   123	  have hν_union (a : α) (ha : a ∈ μ.support) :
   124	      ∑ b ∈ μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support), (ν a).weight b = 1 := by
   125	    apply (hν a ha).weight_sum_eq_one_of_subset
   126	    intro b hb
   127	    exact Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨a, ha, hb⟩
   128	  simp only [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.totalWeight,
   129	    Distribution.bind]
   130	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   131	  calc
   132	    (∑ a ∈ μ.support,
   133	        ∑ b ∈ μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support),
   134	          μ.weight a * (ν a).weight b) =
   135	        ∑ a ∈ μ.support,
   136	          μ.weight a *
   137	            ∑ b ∈ μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support),
   138	              (ν a).weight b := by
   139	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   140	      intro a _
   141	      exact (Finset.mul_sum _ (fun b => (ν a).weight b) (μ.weight a)).symm
   142	    _ = ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a := by
   143	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   144	      intro a ha
   145	      rw [hν_union a ha]
   146	      simp
   147	    _ = 1 := hμ.weight_sum_eq_one

   149	/-- Restrict a distribution to a decidable positive-mass event and normalize it,
   150	as in `def:ith-restricted-line`; blueprint
   151	`ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:600-618`, paper
   152	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1038-1048`. -/
   153	noncomputable def Distribution.restrict {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
   154	    (μ : Distribution α) (p : α → Prop) [DecidablePred p]
   155	    (hpos : 0 < ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight a) : Distribution α where
   156	  support := μ.support.filter p
   157	  weight a := if p a then μ.weight a / ∑ b ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight b else 0
   158	  nonnegative a := by
   159	    split
   160	    · exact div_nonneg (μ.nonnegative a) (le_of_lt hpos)
   161	    · exact le_rfl
   162	  outsideSupport a ha := by
   163	    by_cases hp : p a
   164	    · have hμ : a ∉ μ.support := fun h => ha (Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨h, hp⟩)
   165	      simp [hp, μ.outsideSupport a hμ]
   166	    · simp [hp]

   168	/-- Restriction to a positive-mass event preserves total probability;
   169	`def:ith-restricted-line`, blueprint
   170	`ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:600-618`, paper
   171	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1038-1048`. -/
   172	theorem Distribution.restrict_isProbability {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
   173	    (μ : Distribution α) (p : α → Prop) [DecidablePred p]
   174	    (hpos : 0 < ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight a) :
   175	    (Distribution.restrict μ p hpos).IsProbability := by
   176	  simp only [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.totalWeight,
   177	    Distribution.restrict]
   178	  calc
   179	    (∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p,
   180	        if p a then μ.weight a / ∑ b ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight b else 0) =
   181	        ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p,
   182	          μ.weight a / ∑ b ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight b := by
   183	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   184	      intro a ha
   185	      rw [if_pos (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2]
   186	    _ = (∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight a) /
   187	        ∑ b ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight b := by
   188	      rw [Finset.sum_div]
   189	    _ = 1 := div_self hpos.ne'

   191	/-! ### Push-forwards of finite and uniform distributions
   192	
   193	The results of this section are not named in the paper.  They record the
   194	elementary behaviour of push-forwards of finite distributions, and of uniform
   195	distributions on finite types, that the line-point samplers of the low-degree
   196	game and the identification of question distributions with typed conditionally
   197	linear distributions rely on.
